ingles : War Thunder is a game I’ve been following for many years, having logged over 400 hours on Steam and about 1,000 hours on Xbox. Throughout this extended experience, I’ve observed both the game’s exceptional quality and the challenges that still remain.  Gaijin continues to demonstrate tremendous technical attention to detail in the modeling of aircraft, armored vehicles, and ships. The physics, detailed damage effects, the realism of the Realistic and Simulation modes, and the visual quality of the Dagor Engine make every battle immersive and unique. The photorealistic sky, atmospheric effects, and level of detail in the vehicles are elements that few games can match, and this keeps War Thunder in a special position within the genre.  However, it’s also important to acknowledge the areas that could be improved. The game’s economy, especially for new players, can be demanding and sometimes frustrating. Certain balancing and progression decisions end up affecting matchmaking and the overall experience, particularly at higher tiers. Despite this, it’s fair to mention that Gaijin has been implementing positive changes, such as adjustments to SL gains, changes to repair costs, and greater transparency through the recently published roadmap.  War Thunder remains, for me, a unique and extremely comprehensive experience, but one that benefits from ongoing attention and dialogue with the community. I hope that the announced improvements continue to evolve and that the game increasingly values players’ time and dedication. ------------------------------------------- Portugues: War Thunder é um jogo que acompanho há muitos anos, acumulando mais de 400 horas na Steam e cerca de 1000 horas na Xbox. Ao longo desta experiência prolongada, pude observar tanto a qualidade excecional do jogo como os desafios que ainda persistem.  A Gaijin continua a demonstrar um enorme cuidado técnico na modelação de aeronaves, blindados e navios. A física, os danos detalhados, o realismo dos modos Realístico e Simulação e o trabalho visual do Dagor Engine tornam cada batalha envolvente e única. O céu foto‑realista, os efeitos atmosféricos e o nível de detalhe dos veículos são elementos que poucos jogos conseguem igualar, e isso mantém War Thunder numa posição especial dentro do género.  No entanto, também é importante reconhecer os aspetos que podem ser melhorados. A economia do jogo, especialmente para novos jogadores, pode ser exigente e por vezes frustrante. Certas decisões de balanceamento e progressão acabam por afetar o matchmaking e a experiência geral, sobretudo em tiers mais altos. Apesar disso, é justo mencionar que a Gaijin tem vindo a implementar mudanças positivas, como ajustes nos ganhos de SL, alterações nos custos de reparação e maior transparência através do roadmap publicado recentemente.  War Thunder permanece, para mim, uma experiência única e extremamente completa, mas que beneficia de atenção contínua e diálogo com a comunidade. I wish there was an option to leave a medium review, but I settled on positive because I think that overall, the game has provided me with more enjoyment than displeasure.  Simply put, there is no other game that really does the same thing as war thunder. There is a reason that such a huge community plays it. It's awesome and accessible for people who know nothing about it, but with enough depth for skill expression if you really dive into it. There are all sorts of (mostly) real vehicles with decently accurate (within reason) specs and functionality, especially so at the lower ranks. With the ability to play naval, ground, and air there is most likely the ability for anyone to find something they enjoy in the game  Personally, War Thunder is what got me interested in combat aviation. I remember watching the movie The Wind Rises, and coming home and downloading this game so I could play the zeros I saw in the movie. I played arcade for a long time, hopped between a few nations before settling as the british for a long time. I tried RB, but bounced off it and didn't put in the time to learn it, so I sloooowly grinded through the british air tree.  Several years later, a friend of mine saw me playing and was interested in trying it. I of course, obliged and we played a bit of arcade together. we both got really into the game and would play it together all the time.  We learned together, we talked about plane specs, plane strengths, and tried real maneuvers together. We both grinded from reserve russian planes to about rank 5, the early jets. This is where we split a little bit. I really wanted to get to top tier. I think jets are really cool, but he had recently found the enjoyment he was looking for in the tier 4ish prop game.  We both got the 37D Viggen premium, so we instantly were able to play rank 8 with fox 3s. We would play it from time to time, but I went on to buy more top tier premiums while he kept going back and just grinding lower ranks up to the BR he liked, and then moving on.  In the end, this game is better when you find what you enjoy in it. Hopefully it's not top tier. My friend got his enjoyment out of the game, and found what he enjoyed, got what he wanted out of it, and as far as I know, has practically quit the game. Life moves on. As for me, I stayed playing it for a long time. I have purchased 18 packs from the war thunder store. I have spent hundreds on golden eagles. I've bought several Premiums outside of the packs (12) , as well as premium time. It's not reasonable to play top tier at all without premium by the way, you will almost always run at a SL deficit. I always had to go and ground pound for SL, while my friend who played props for fun, always had an abundance of SL, and since he wasn't chasing the next plane, he didn't need to spend it, or grind whatever he didn't care about  Ground and naval is kind of the same story if you like that kind of stuff  Long story short, Play this game if you're interested in biplanes-early jets. If you go further than that, you should be prepared to shell out money, or an exorbitant amount of time. This isn't hyperbole, without premium, a premium vehicle, and GL to speed your research up, you're probably spending easily years of regular play to reach top tier. The devs have been leaning more and more towards extracting as much money as they can out of players, so don't give them the satisfaction

War thunder is incredible one month and terrible the next. I've been playing the game for 13 years with a close friend, we feel like dinosaurs in the current game. Here are some of the outstanding issues I have seen first hand, I will come back to update my review of the game however in it's current state I do not recommend it, especially for new players.   I am only going to address the Tank or “combined battles” mode in this review, there are a LOT of things wrong and I can not address them all in this, it honestly needs a video review and there are other issues in the Air and the now incredibly dead naval mode. These are the big 3 for me right now.  Tank or Combined battle's issues   “Wallet Warriors” - Gaijin has added premium vehicles ($80 at top tier for 1 vehicle for 1 country). People are encouraged to buy these since they make the grind easier. At top tier the majority of these vehicles are better than standard tech tree variants (some are worse and outright scams). The biggest issue that is never addressed is that people will buy an top tier vehicle with no idea how to play the game, spawn in ground with their 1 vehicle, immediately be killed and leave the match. The game is designed so that in combined battles players must bring 3-5 tanks and 1-2 aircrafts etc. etc. so the match can be played out. Wallet Warriors have flooded the American, and Russian tress (the 2 largest) spawn, die, leave and throw the match instantly, this is extremely prevalent at top tier. Gaijin attempted to fix this by giving tankers free vehicles to encourage them to keep going at top tier however these players either do not care or understand the game and have actively made the top tier experience unplayable.   Map size and Game Modes - At top tier you have tanks designed and capable of killing other tanks at 2-3+ km or more. However, most maps are less than 2km in size. Most engagements in the game are at less than 100 meters. Gaijin decided to take somewhat decent map designs and stretch them or make 1 cap king of the hill or 2 cap “capture enemy base” style modes. 1 cap maps are impossible to play, they leave large sections of the maps where there is no objective for people to conduct insane flanks not to play the objective but to spawn camp. The 1 cap is often in the middle of a field or something with no cover which encourages players to find angles to kill players attempting to actually play the objective effectively turning an objective based mode into team death match. The 2 cap system is even worse, I encourage anyone reading this to google a picture of a War Thunder 2 cap map. The objectives are placed in each teams spawn and require 3 minutes to decap the point and 3 minutes of actively sitting and holding the point (regardless of friendly vehicles inside the objective the timer still moves the same) inside the enemy spawns to capture it. This is an IMPOSSIBLE task and only can be done once you have effectively permanently killed enough members of the enemy team sending them back to the hangar (lobby). I can not began to explain how horrific the War thunder ground map designs are, most of  them are based on real locations or ideas of them which is extremely cool. However 9/10 of them have designs where 1 team can shoot into the other teams spawn with an advantage at the start of the match, or if they capture 1 point or hill they can shoot into the other teams spawn. The amount of spawn camping in this game I think causes a lot of mental stress on the community.   A Solution to the Map size and game modes would be to double the map size at top tier (already done btw) and double the player count. At top tier with the current player count and the wallet warriors immediately leaving, if you're on 3 cap you cap a point and drive around for 10-15 minutes looking for enemies and eventually migrate to either their spawn or another point where someone will be holding a hill or angle and just eliminate you.   Helicopters  - Helicopters were introduced very poorly into war thunder and still have not been implemented well. They were originally added as a separate tree where you would have to play a low tier helicopter and grind for higher ones, however if you spent the entire game in a helicopter you would receive very little to no XP or research points for the next one making the grind insanely long. Helicopters when first introduced could also spawn with full ATGMs (Anti tank guided missiles) at the beginning of the round, most players would just spawn and fly to an angle on the enemy tank spawn and fire off 12-16 missiles and get a few kills. This was encouraged because it would be the most dense area of enemy tanks and most SPAA players do not leave the spawn, therefore if you do not want to be shot down as a helicopter you MUST spawn camp to stop the SPAA threat. The SPAA system has not gotten better, it arguably has gotten worse with multi spawn vehicles and radars that can see through mountains and hills. SPAA players are encouraged to not leave the spawn and if anything to drive away from the battlefield (yes backwards from their spawn) to just fire on Aircrafts all game. The new SPAA systems can even effectively shoot down incoming missiles. I understand its a game and some things are not realistic, but a BUK 3 firing 16 multi million dollar missiles to engage 16 hellfire's would bankrupt any country.   A fix for helicopters would be to give them a scouting ability like drones and light tanks to better support the team. A dedicated point for helicopters or aircrafts to capture that only helicopters or aircrafts can capture, this would help with helicopter grinding and provide a unique aspect to the combined battles. I think helicopters especially at top tier that do not have the spike, PARs 3 and LMUR style missiles should be able to spawn first with ATGMs. I think SPAA’s should have a dedicated spawn somewhere off to the side of the battlefield away from the main tank spawns to prevent blatant spawn camping and SPAA players from hiding and dragging out a match when the game has been won.

War Thunder Review – A Frustrating Grind with Glimmers of Fun  War Thunder is an okay game overall, but the experience heavily depends on your battle rating (BR). Low tiers up to around 9.0 are genuinely fun. After that, however, it becomes absolute hell.  The matchmaking is the biggest culprit. Out of 20 games, I’ve only had about 2 that were actually at my own tier; the rest are full uptiers. So, don't expect historically accurate battles—at top tier (12.7), it plays like Call of Duty, but somehow worse.  My main gripes with the grind come down to a few critical issues:  Outdated & Tiny Maps: We have weapons capable of engaging targets from 1 to 120 kilometers away, yet we are still fighting on cramped 1x1 km squares. To make matters worse, the game modes are practically identical to what we've had since 2016. We rarely get true combined arms gameplay on the large maps that would actually make those long-range weapons viable.  Overpriced Premiums: Premium vehicles and accounts are far too expensive for the lack of meaningful innovation the company puts into the core gameplay.  Relentless Uptiers & CAS: Uptiers feel more recurrent than ever before. If you're a new player, prepare to be killed by planes constantly. Your only options are to get exceptionally good with SPAA or grind out a plane of your own just to fight back.  The "One-Death Leaver" Epidemic: This is a massive problem. Even when players are given free backup vehicles, they still leave after one death because there are no real consequences for abandoning the match—unlike in Enlisted, where the system penalizes you much more harshly.  Verdict: Fun at low tiers, but the constant uptiers, stale map design, and lack of consequences for leavers make the higher tiers an exercise in frustration.

Game can be fun, but those matches are quite rare.  In Ground RB (what this review is mostly about) you can often tell the outcome of the game within the first minute or two of game play depending on who pushes harder and who collapses first.  Add in unbalanced tanks and CAS and it makes for a literal slaughter for the enemy team.  Even if you are on the winning team its not fun as there is 0 challenge except the occasional few players who try their best to fight it out (appreciate you guys).  Suggestions: Relook at balancing of various vehicles T-72 @ 9.3? while Sho't Kal Dalet is a 9.0 what are you even thinking, one of those is a literal potato with tracks.  Many of vehicles of all types have BRs that are clearly to high or two low, premium or not.  Take community feedback and actually use it.  Don't just be like "yeah its broken so we will leave it like that for a month or forever"  Incorporate some sort of system to attempt to balance games vs the lack of anything currently.  Yes people will complaining about some basic skill based match making but realistically it should exist at some level, it can be implemented smartly.  Its awful if you get a bunch of e-sports ready gamers on the enemy team in one match, then the next match you get people who don't understand basic controls or want to go sight seeing.  I wish that was a joke.  People who queue up with 1 tank or 1 tank + CAS, put them into a queue where they will only match up with others who play like that.  So often this people get killed early on and your or the enemy team are down several people which will throw the game.  Not every game needs to be a challenge where its down to the wire, but as it stands right now no matter what side you are on, winning or loosing.  Its just a crappy experience.  Also Yak-130 should probably move up to 10.0 / 10.3.  Its flight performance with 4x TV guided bombs is unmatched by anything other countries have, heck the A-4E needs rocket boosters to help take off, and the Hunter F.58's maneuverability is not all that great.  Oh one last think.  BR brackets for match making should be tightened.  Instead of +/- 1.0 (which is 3 BR ranks), maybe it 2 BR ranks instead.  For example, you queue @ 9.0, your max match making would be between 8.3 and 9.7.  This will also help keep vehicles from facing stuff they have zero hope of countering.  More game modes would be cool too.  I like what we got, but some more new stuff would be great.  Not gonna lie the more I enjoy playing a game, the more I'm willing to spend on either skins or vehicle packs.

War Thunder is a game with an incredibly ambitious concept and an impressive amount of content, but after spending a significant amount of time playing it, I found that its strengths are consistently overshadowed by frustrating design decisions. While it excels in historical authenticity, vehicle variety, and realistic combat mechanics, the overall experience becomes increasingly difficult to enjoy due to its progression system, balance issues, and heavy emphasis on monetization.  One of the game's greatest achievements is its enormous collection of military vehicles. Players have access to hundreds of aircraft, tanks, helicopters, and naval vessels from numerous nations, many of which are recreated with an impressive level of detail. The sound design, vehicle models, and damage mechanics demonstrate the amount of effort that has gone into creating an immersive battlefield. At its best, War Thunder delivers tense, rewarding encounters where positioning, map knowledge, and tactical decision-making genuinely matter. Those moments are exciting and memorable, showing the potential of what the game can be.  Unfortunately, these positive aspects are often overshadowed by an exhausting progression system. Advancing through the technology trees becomes increasingly time-consuming as players reach higher ranks. Research costs continue to increase, vehicle modifications require substantial amounts of experience, and earning enough in-game currency to purchase and maintain vehicles can become a challenge. While the game can technically be enjoyed without spending money, progression frequently feels slow enough that premium accounts, premium vehicles, and various boosters appear less like optional conveniences and more like practical necessities. This creates the impression that the game prioritizes extending player engagement and encouraging purchases rather than providing consistently rewarding progression.  Another recurring issue is matchmaking and overall game balance. Although the battle rating system is intended to create fair matches, the actual gameplay experience can vary dramatically from one battle to the next. Certain vehicles significantly outperform others within the same rating range, leading to encounters where victory feels determined more by equipment than by strategy or player skill. New content and balance updates occasionally shift the competitive landscape, but they do not always resolve long-standing concerns. As a result, many matches can feel inconsistent, with players alternating between highly competitive games and battles that seem unwinnable from the very beginning.  The learning curve presents an additional challenge, particularly for new players. War Thunder contains a remarkable amount of depth, including armor penetration mechanics, shell selection, crew qualifications, ammunition storage, vehicle weak points, map positioning, and numerous nation-specific characteristics. However, the game offers relatively limited guidance on these systems. New players are often expected to learn through repeated trial and error or by consulting external guides created by the community. This lack of effective onboarding can make the early experience unnecessarily discouraging, especially when facing opponents with significantly more knowledge and experience.  Technical and gameplay issues further reduce the overall experience. Server instability, occasional bugs, inconsistent hit registration, and unexpected balance adjustments can interrupt otherwise enjoyable matches. In addition, the in-game economy has undergone numerous changes over the years, many of which have generated significant debate within the community. Adjustments to repair costs, research rewards, and progression often leave players feeling that their time investment is not adequately rewarded.  Perhaps the most disappointing aspect of War Thunder is that its problems stem not from a lack of potential, but from decisions surrounding its long-term design philosophy. The core gameplay remains engaging, the historical attention to detail is exceptional, and the combined-arms combat system is unlike almost anything else available. However, these strengths are repeatedly undermined by excessive grinding, monetization systems that feel increasingly prominent, inconsistent balancing, and a progression model that often prioritizes player retention over player satisfaction.  In conclusion, War Thunder is a title that demonstrates remarkable ambition and technical achievement, but it struggles to provide an equally satisfying overall experience. Players who are willing to dedicate hundreds or even thousands of hours—or invest additional money into premium content—may discover a deeply engaging military simulation with virtually endless content. For many others, however, the repetitive progression, uneven matchmaking, and persistent grind can overshadow the game's undeniable strengths. Despite its impressive foundation, War Thunder ultimately feels like a game whose greatest obstacle is not its gameplay, but the systems built around it.

10/10 – 424 Hours and I'm Still Hooked  I've put 424 hours into War Thunder, playing mostly Realistic Battles with the USA, Germany, and a little Russia, focusing mainly on tanks with some aircraft mixed in.  There's just something about this game that scratches an itch no other game does. The realism is incredible, and the tank gameplay is easily the best I've experienced. Watching a round penetrate armor, seeing the spalling and internal damage, and having every shot matter makes each fight feel rewarding. The damage models are fantastic, and every engagement feels different depending on where you hit your opponent.  Is it perfect? No.  The grind can definitely be rough, especially at higher ranks. But when you finally unlock that next vehicle you've been working toward, the feeling is worth it. It makes the progression feel meaningful instead of just handing everything to you.  Spawn camping can also be frustrating, but if we're being honest... we've all been guilty of it at some point. It's part of the game, even if it isn't always fun to be on the receiving end.  I've spent money on the game, but you don't have to in order to enjoy it. There are a handful of premium vehicles that can feel a little overpowered, but none of them have been enough to ruin the experience for me.  After 424 hours, I still find myself coming back because no other game delivers combined-arms combat with this level of realism and satisfaction. If you're willing to learn, be patient with the grind, and enjoy tactical gameplay, War Thunder is absolutely worth your time.  10/10. I recommend this game 10,000%.

If you're looking for a break from all the first person shooters, and a new skillset to master this is it. Tank battles are personally a bit boring if you're coming from that FPS scene, but Aircraft PvP is where it's at, mastering the art of dogfighting was definitely a big challenge, but once you get a grip of the basics the game becomes very satisfying to outwit your opponent off of skill alone. You might have heard of counterstrafing & jigglepeeking, but get ready to be awed by the wide range of tactics known as energyfighting, managing potential & kinetic energy, ACMs, Boom & Zoom tactics, rope-a-dopes, High Yo-Yos, reversals, and rolling-scissors to name a few interesting tactics. There is literally an ENDLESS list of tactics to learn, you could never be bored playing this game. (Maybe frustrated dying over and over, but eventually once you'll 'get it', it's very enjoyable to best your enemy in aerial combat.)  To be honest, a very hard game to recommend to people, mainly because this game attracts a alot of far-right leaning/politically ignorant people (particular with ground vehicles, not so much air vehicles) so some non-fans might look at you the wrong way. But don't get me wrong there's a bunch of chill people that just play the game for the funs. Other reviews probably leave alot of complaints about the game's balance, I'll leave it to them, but overall if you want to get a particular vehicle of interest, you might have to pay money, otherwise it's lot of time spent trying to grind up. But if you look past that, there's alot of fun to be had in mastering the skills and quirks of some of the lesser known aircraft that might not all be that famous as there's definitely some underrated & amazing eggs to be piloted.

Your weapon and plane matter a LOT which makes choosing planes very cool      [*] The variety of vehicles is insane. In my 100 hours I didn't even come close to running out of content to work towards. I barely even scratched the surface      [*] The gameplay offers a variety and a mix of playstyles. [*] Learning this game can be super rewarding. There is so much in depth simulation for each aircraft that you can almost learn how to actually fly just by playing this game      [*] Arcade and realistic can both be fun, although realistic air is a bit too unforgiving. It's definitely a playstyle and rewarding to get kills but it feels awful to fly for 15 minutes after being in queue for 4 just to get one tapped out of nowhere [/list]  [h3] Now onto the CONS since I've ran out of nice things to say [/h3]  [list]     [*] The game [b] HEAVILY [/b] Emphasis pay to win or pay to progress. Progress is INSANELY slow even early game, and around tier 3 or 4. You have to start performing top 3 every match AND winning to even break a profit as a fully free player. There are also just some insanely broken premium vehicles that you will see almost every match at their rank      [*] Pay to win Part 2: Pricing edition. The vehicles in this game are also insanely over priced for virtual planes. 10 bucks for a plane is kinda pushing it for me but  [b] 80 DOLLARS FOR ONE VEHICLE[/b] is ABSURD. You are not only paying for a better vehicle most of the time, but you are also getting a massive reward in terms of currency and the cherry on top is you do not even have to OWN a vehicle in that tier or research this option. It is simply given to you immediately. If you want to be even remotely serious about this game in the long run, you are basically forced to get a premium at one point.      [*] Pay to win Part 4: "Vehicle Diversity" edition. Warthunder loves to claim that it has "Over 2500 vehicles" as one of it's main selling points. However, what they neglect to mention is that roughly half to a third of these vehicles are premium. There are a few tech trees that almost have more PREMIUM vehicles than normal! For example, Russians have a plane that turns faster than Japan fighters, Has better ammunition than Germany, Has better fire rate than US AND Has a decent climb and low altitude performance. That plane is the START PLANE, and it out performs up to 2 full tiers ahead of itself. You will genuinely have to base your plane picks around the Russian options in the game or you will just reserve yourself to dying to them about 90% of the time. You can't even test fly the plane until you're already a research behind it on the tree! Giving you NO chance of possibly knowing if you're about to waste 250+ hours grinding to that plane. I started playing War Thunder in January 2014. I'm currently Level 92 with 992 hours of playtime.  First of all, I'm pretty sure that playtime displayed on the War Thunder website can't be correct—the displayed hours are definitely not my actual total playtime. Don't mind the playtime on steam since I just recently started to open the game not by it's own launcher.  The core concept of the game is genuinely excellent, and War Thunder has a lot of great aspects.  BUT  There are simply too many things that completely ruin the overall experience.  - The biggest issue: In virtually every single match, you're placed in battles against vehicles that are up to—and most of the time exactly—one full Battle Rating higher than your own. This constant uptiering creates extremely unfair matchups, making it nearly impossible to compete against certain vehicles. Since these vehicles also exist in some form for almost every nation, often including captured versions, you encounter them in nearly every match across almost every Battle Rating, leaving you at a constant disadvantage.  - The second biggest issue: Aircraft in Ground Realistic Battles are complete match killers and ruin every kill streak you manage to build. In literally every match, you get bombed multiple times. As soon as you destroy an enemy, they'll be back less than 30 seconds later in an aircraft, using the kill cam to know your exact location before dropping a bomb directly on you.  - The grind is completely excessive. The number of hours required to unlock a specific vehicle or aircraft is absurd. Unless you pay for Premium or spend significant amounts of money, it takes forever to unlock anything new. The higher the tier, the longer the grind becomes. It's a typical free-to-play problem.  - Many vehicles are only obtainable through events or by purchasing them. If you want to buy just a single, average tank, you'll easily end up paying around 80 Swiss Francs. In most cases, these vehicles are released in an overpowered state, only to be repeatedly nerfed shortly afterward until they're no longer worth the price.  - The map rotation has almost no variety. Out of all the maps in the game, you only ever play a small handful, while the majority rarely appear—if at all, usually only at top tier. Some maps are even restricted to specific Battle Ratings, meaning you can only play them for a limited portion of your progression before they disappear from the rotation.  - Many maps also have alternate versions with only one or two capture points instead of the usual three. The single-capture-point versions, in particular, provide an absolutely terrible gameplay experience.  - Spawns are not properly protected. Spawn rushing happens in virtually every single match. Even when it doesn't, spawn protection feels completely inconsistent and ends so abruptly that you're often bombed immediately after spawning or spawn-camped from a distance without even having the chance to leave your spawn.  - The user interface has become worse with every redesign. Finding settings is unnecessarily difficult, and much of the game's content isn't explained at all. There are countless features that remain undiscovered, inaccessible, or simply unusable because they're hidden away in confusing menus or blocked by bugs.  - Customer support is effectively non-existent. You rarely receive a response, and reporting players appears to accomplish nothing.  - The in-game chat is nothing but a constant stream of insults and toxicity. Getting flamed for no reason has become completely normal.  - Players on your own team can physically push your vehicle around. If your tank is lighter or weaker, there's often nothing you can do except destroy your own vehicle to escape. Even then, the same player can simply repeat the exact same behavior after your next respawn.  These are just a hand full of negative aspects in the game.  War Thunder has a fantastic concept buried underneath layers of frustrating game design, aggressive monetization, and poor balancing. In its current state, it feels less like a game designed to be enjoyable and more like one designed to keep players grinding and spending money.  To make matters worse, the game also requires an enormous amount of storage space.

"Ma'am, the weirdos on Reddit are getting out of hand."  If I had a nickel for every time I've seen this game's community attempt another campaign of extreme amounts of review bombing, I'd have like 90 nickels at this point. Review bombing as a one off tactic to protest a genuinely *bad* thing is fine and should be encouraged, but now the community will review bomb over anything, even something as genuinely trivial as a 30mm plate of steel...  I'll be genuine- the game is extremely grindy. With no premium account or vehicles, the an "average" player will reach a Rank IX aircraft or Rank VIII ground vehicle in around 3-4 months if they play nonstop. This is comparable, roughly, to World of Tanks- your mileage *will* vary, and it heavily depends on your skill. If you're not great at the game, this time will increase exponentially, but you'll also learn to play the game somewhat in the process, making it faster as time goes on.  Premium vehicle spam is a problem, but not as severe as many players would have you believe from how hard they bash it. The average War Thunder redditor is not representative of the average community experience, and this issue is no different; many of them will complain about what they've dubbed "copy paste slop", premium vehicles that are statistically identical to an already existing tech tree or premium vehicle in the game, with a common target of this criticism being the Leopard 2A4 (and its extremely large number of subvariants)- this is genuinely stupid. Only a few vehicles feel like genuine copy paste and can actually be *identified* as such, like the very unfortunate state of affairs of the Saab J 35 XS (you can see they never fixed the light map and camo and so it has a gap for Swedish roundels but has Finnish ones). Does it suck when that happens? Yes. Is it worth being a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? No.  """Russian bias""" as the extremely vocal minority of the community likes to say it, is... well, not as biased as you'd believe. On average, Russian vehicles perform par or worse than their BLUFOR contemporaries, and in a number of cases have caught nerf bats to the skulls when they overperform beyond actual expectation. Most people who do complain about Russian bias are the same types of people who play with 250ms of ping and complain about ghost shells doing nothing, and then promptly die to a player who actually knows what strategic positioning is. Russian vehicles in War Thunder are unironically tuned to perform par with BLUFOR because if BLUFOR was in War Thunder at the actual documented technological advanceness and effectiveness we know many BLUFOR nations are at... well, Russia's winrate would be less than 30%- this directly contradicts one of Gaijin's balancing statement. Sorry America mains, no M829A4- sorry Germany mains, no DM63- sorry Euro mains, no millimeter wave radar guided Brimstones.  Would I recommend the game... well, despite what the little box I checked would say, it really kinda just depends. The game is fundamentally in no way bad- it's just that it has a very steep learning curve, and a large number of its parts can leave some people feeling that the sum is terrible. I would say, *try* the game first and formulate personal first opinions that aren't influenced by the reviews, because the reviews are rarely reflective of the actual quality of the game, and if you happen to like the game in the first few hours, then great! If not, then it's not a big deal and you only lost a couple hours playing.

When I first started this game, I thought it was nothing but fantastic. Having spent a bit of time in it, I've come to the conclusion that this game was a huge waste of time and money.  The specific mechanics in this game are fantastic. It has some of the best physics (for the most part) and weapon simulation out of any military game across the board. Comparing to something like a true simulation, it's not quite as detailed or realistic but it makes up for it in the sheer volume of different vehicles available.  Now, the problem is the grind, the lack of care for the players, and the clear driving force behind almost every decision made; MONEY. I get this game is f2p and they need to make money, but everything in this is so egregious and aggressively monetized that it just isn't fun. For example, I'm a huge fan of quirky planes like the Harrier, Spitfire, and F111, and enjoy fast pased action gameplay. This game has all of that and more. The problem is actually playing the game. If, like me, you are a fan of Cold War to modern era jets, good luck. It will take you 500 hours to reach them, as I have only gotten to the high end just recently. There are a number of videos calculating how long it will take to finish the trees. Another issue, they are only adding content which extends the grind, and now adding an infantry mode which will have entirely separate trees. This will all MASSIVELY inflate grind. All while having gamemodes that are all essentially death match with no strategic objectives or any kind of depth to the missions. There is no desire or care to improve, only to add for money.  There are a number of issues with balance as well, like premium vehicles being near indestructible, overbearingly powerful, or both (KV-2, BMPT, etc). Also accuracy with time-frame of a vehicle and BR being compressed or incorrect for a given vehicle.  I had to stop playing this game because I realized it just wasn't fun. The player-base is super toxic, the game is one of the most predatory I have ever seen, and I felt like I was just staring at a list of super expensive vehicles while being coerced into shelling out money to use the vehicles I want.

Starting this off with the good things, as they are abundant yet outnumbered by the bad. War Thunder has a great, vast selection of historical tanks, planes and ships; some prototype, some service; some vehicles weren't even built like the Panther II, Maus, E100 among many, many others. The combat systems, although they leave much to desire, are for the most part realistic and fair. There isn't much RNG to the penetration systems; a 37mm WW1-WW2 solid shot round won't penetrate a modern MBT no matter where it is shot, for the most part. I cannot speak for planes or battleships because I do not play them.   The game also has quite the historically accurate statistics for most vehicles. There are some inconsistencies but they are less abundant than correct. Models for tanks, planes and ships look very close to their real life counter parts, and have the same modules as they would in real life, such as more modern SPAA guns having different generations and types of radars, among other things. There are also for the most part realistic engine names, such as the prototype M6A1 having a variant of the C-W R-1820 Cyclone, which was used in the B-17 and P-36 most notably.   There are more positives, but they are much smaller and less significant than historical accuracies and inaccuracies. The GUI for example is simple for the most part and easy to navigate, and the game isn't particularly pay to win, but that will be touched on in a moment.   Starting off with the many negatives, which there are many, will be the situation with premium tanks and planes. I will start this off by saying I am a Ground RB player so I cannot speak for Air & Naval Arcade/RB/SIM, or Ground Arcade/SIM. The majority of the lesser known prototype tanks, planes, variants alike are premiums, available through events, premium currencies or bundles bought with real life currency. Examples include: E-100, Maus, IA.58 Pucura, Object 279, KV-1B, M6A2E1, AMX Surblinde and more. These tanks (and plane) that have been listed, some are incredibly rare and overpowered. The M6A2E1, Surblinde and Object 279 are in the price range well above 800 USD(?), with the Object 279 being the most expensive of the three being over 1500 USD(?) The Gaijin Market uses their own currency but I believe the conversion is 1 GC - 1 USD, I could be wrong. Either way, these premiums are incredibly expensive especially for how they perform.   The IA.58 Pucura is a new to the game, late 20th century turbo prop aircraft that gets dozens of anti-tank rockets, at a relatively low battle rating. At 4.7 in Ground RB it fights M4 Shermans, T-34s, KV-1s, among other WW2 tanks. It's rockets have the ability to one shot pretty much every single tank it can face at that BR, and higher. It is also an incredible dog fighter, as is shown in a YouTube video by Spookston. It can dog fight with P-51s, P-36s and Yak series planes just fine, while being much more durable and with better firepower.  Moving on from the overpowered premiums, there is the case of absurdly priced vehicles. As spoken on earlier, there are vehicles worth hundreds of dollars on the market, which is mostly player driven. The vehicles, which are mostly modern MBTs or IFVs, are in bundles. Most of these bundles contain 1-3 vehicles ranging from 40 dollars to 80 for them. The majority of these bundles are copy-paste vehicles, such as the newer Senrai Maidens pack, which contains modern MBTs from the U.S, Germany, USSR and Britain. These tanks are direct reskins of other premiums, in color and paint schemes of made up anime girls. Anime girls. There are also Gemini AI watermarks on them, along with other camouflages added previously.  Aside from all the absurdly priced premiums and packs, the core gameplay is also a major issue. There are a lot of bugs, some small, some quite literally battle turning and game breaking. Bugs from tank parts flying in the air, disappearing, or unremovable fire in places a plane crashed, to visual glitches mimicking graphics card failure, rounds completely disappearing/going through a vehicle without doing any damage or even registering, and certain areas/maps causing major FPS drops to the point where it can be unplayable. Not to mention the fact that the game can crash whenever it would like, or start lagging uncontrollably.   Certain gameplay systems such as Volumetric armor cause more problems than they should. Volumetric can make it so your round could just... fail to penetrate. Shooting a blatant weak-spot on a tank can result in a failure to penetrate just because this system incorrectly guesses how it would penetrate. There are times volumetric can cause certain parts of tanks to be in the thousands of millimeters thick, such as the driver ports on most German medium-heavy tanks; for example: the Panzer IV, and all variants of the Tigers.   Machine gun ports can do the same thing. Some parts of the ports can have 900-2000mm of armor where it should have.. maybe 100-150. This is due to volumetric believing the length of said part is actual armor thickness. On the T-34 series of tanks, there is a lip extending from the side of the tank, above the track, which if hit right, can result in a non-pen with a modern MBT APFSDS dart, because volumetric believes that lip is part of the structural armor of the tank, thus making it react like, for example, the upper front plate.  The community is a large part of why the game is seen poorly. The majority of the community has atleast a thousand hours in the game, and are incredibly toxic and will quite literally do anything for an advantage. If you have ever used the internet, you know that the community for War Thunder has a track record of leaking classified military documents just to prove a point, have an advantage in a certain vehicle or give a disadvantage to another. The community also plays the game as seriously as possible; I have seen videos of people literally crying because they died in game. Not complaining, crying; tears and all. There is also a 70% chance they spawn a plane to revenge kill you, or specifically hunt you down to kill you. They get so angry and hateful if you do better than them that they will stop at no line to ruin your experience. I myself have killed level 100s with 10000+ hours, and been called racial slurs, some I didn't even know were slurs.  Despite Gaijin's horrible track record and the overwhelming hatred among the community, every time a new premium, pack, paid feature, or literally anything is released, people flock to the game and buy said thing, or spend hours to get it. The day the IA.58 Pucura was released, it had sold hundreds of times and literally every 4.7 match was guaranteed to have at least three of them. There were so many of these planes at one point that the only thing you could see in the sky was this one plane. When the Hummel, a German Artillery tank, was added (same update as Pucura), there were at least 5 of them on the German team. Playing Germany, if you looked at the scoreboard, the majority of tanks were Hummels.  I believe it is a good game. The game can be fun, realistic for the most part and has plenty of content. Everyone should at least play it once, but, the majority of new players quit within their first 24 hours of gameplay, purely because of the grind, the majorly sweaty community, horrible optimization or lack of knowledge. This is not a game that you can learn easily, and the tutorials are incredibly vague, only teaching you how to aim, shoot, move and some small key binds, then throws you in without any explanation.   TL-DR: There are more positives and negatives, but one can only list so many pros and cons while remaining sane. The game is quite historically accurate and has an abundance of content, thousands of hours worth at the least, but it also has incredibly major flaws, most being completely experience ruining. The community is one of the worst in gaming, or at least close to it.

War Thunder is, without a doubt, a technical masterpiece. The vehicle detail, physics, and sheer depth of the combat are unmatched in the current market. I’ve genuinely enjoyed the core gameplay, and it’s why I’ve stuck with it for as long as I have. However, I can no longer recommend it to newcomers without a major caveat: the progression economy. The grind isn’t a natural challenge, it feels like a calculated barrier. After reaching the mid tiers, you quickly realize that the game is tuned to create low reward multipliers, punishing repair costs, and stock grinds, that intentionally forces players toward the store to buy their way out of frustration. What’s most concerning is that this isn't just a War Thunder issue. It is the signature (Gaijin Formula) we see repeated across their other titles like Crossout and Enlisted. They build a brilliant, addictive core game and then wrap it in a monetization model that devalues the player's time to drive microtransactions. I want to see War Thunder thrive because of its gameplay, not because it successfully milks its player base through FOMO and artificial bottlenecks. If you are a fan of war machinery, the game is a 10/10. But until the economy respects the time we put into the game, it is very hard to recommend this as a hobby rather than a financial chore.

Further compounding the above issue.  -The developers taking a very inconsistent attitude to implementation of the vehicles in game. Adding things like missiles to some aircraft that were only ever tested on them but not deployed operationally while others will at times not get missiles they actually used for "balance," despite the game being a generally unbalanced mess that gives you the impression no one on the dev team actually plays the game they make.    -Game modes - The base game is basically COD style team death match in tanks or planes (Naval is a thing but practically abandoned and ignore.) There are game modes that were teased back in 2014 (Enduring Confrontation) that they at most had a few tests on than largely ignored. -- For tanks this means modern battle tanks in what is essentially 1.5km square maps for a good chunk of top BR cod style twitch death matches with the occasional camper sitting and waiting for people to cross their sight lines. -- For aircraft this means anything that isn't a fighter is just an XP piniata. Don't play this game expecting to get much use out of the bombers and attackers in its vehicle roster.  There has been some headway on new game modes but its mostly driven by community outrage at 12 years of the same basic game modes and probably fear of games like Nuclear Option being an option for the playerbase to move to and leave this game.  -The Grind. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it has only gotten worse and worse through the years with the devs doing their measured best to make it as slow and painful as possible, even with a premium account, to encourage people to spend money. There are vehicles implemented with issues and when bug reports get made on them the developers will ignore them for years until they have a $60-80 premium to sell to the community. Latest case in point, the F-14D Super Tomcat and a premium M60 tank get announced and suddenly they care about fixing the AIM-54 phoenix's and the M60 Mantlet armor.  Needless to say the game needs serious balance passes, new game modes and the developers need to stop making decisions on only whatever can make them a quick buck. What was once a cherishable gaming experience has now turned into a frustrating grind fest with nothing but disappointment for veteran and new players alike. The selling point that Gaijin proudly presents is that the game is free and yes to a certain degree that statement is true, however if you play the game long enough you'll begin to see that a free game like War Thunder has it's catch, many of which Gaijin seems to get away with.  Let's start with one of the biggest concerns and outrage the community is having to deal with right now, the premium prices. The game relies on a progression system built to have you work your way down tech trees to earn better and stronger vehicles to purchase, however it's design is made to feel endless unless you're willing to sacrifice payments to buy premium time so you can make the grind "slightly" easier. Other ways to bypass this problem is to purchase a premium vehicle for an easier, engaging exprience but even then nobody is wanting to pay 80-100$ CAD (More or less depending on your currency) to fill in this gap. Even with sales ranging from 30% all the way up to 50% these packs aren't justified into buying for the sake of the price alone. The greed needs to be put aside with Gaijin coming to a conclusion on how to make store purchases more afforable for the average player.  But if you're willing to look past these absurd prices and give into the snails demands, you will find that most of these premiums are nothing short of copy and paste vehicles from there respective trees, like the BMPT-72, The Clickbait, T-80 and many more. Nothing is truly unique anymore, it's just a means to an end, a shortcut for players who aren't willing to grind their way to the top. It's no mystery to wonder why you see so many new players who have barely scratched rank 15, going into the 10.7 to 12.0 bracket, using these premiums and leaving after one death. But despite these shortcomings, you will also find that a lot of these premiums seem to have balancing issues, whether they're blatantly overpowered and providing you with a strong advantage or weak and underwhelming (The former of which always seems to be the case).  Second issue we're starting to see is the amount of AI usage Gaijin is putting into the game. Textures, Artwork, etc. It's a lazy effort to make the developers jobs easier rather than hiring artist and programmers who have a passion and drive to make the game a better experience with their work for everyone. Players are willing to put in the hours if they are playing a product that has actual creative value from it's developers rather than a machine generating the slop that we're receiving currently. The "Senrai Maidens" packs are a prime example of the lengths Gaijin is willing to go for an easy quick buck, just lazy, copy and paste, AI slop.  In conclusion, the community is wanting to be heard. We're starting to push back from these choices and time after time, Gaijin is choosing to either ignore it or give a tone deaf response to all the criticism they are receiving. No longer are we wanting to stand for what we are being given, we want a change, not only to the statements listed above but to several recurring issues that the community has been dealing with these last few years. It's only a matter of time till these issues cause the game to completely die and have even the most loyal of players stop playing for good. I'd like to be optimistic in hopes that change can be brought forth so we can begin to see the game in a healthier state for a more enjoyable experience among the community. So let these reviews be a wake up call to Gaijin before it's too late.

I'm not exaggerating when i say this is probably the worst gaming experience when you actually learn how the game works.  The biggest problem is the obvious Russian bias. Whether it's damage models, survivability, BR placement, or how quickly certain vehicles get nerfed or buffed, it often feels like Russian vehicles get preferential treatment. Even if every individual case can be explained away, the overall pattern has become impossible to ignore for many veteran players.  Then there's the progression system. It isn't designed to reward your time, it's designed to sell premium accounts, premium vehicles, and premium currency. Once you reach the mid-to-high tiers, progression slows to a crawl unless you're paying. Repair costs, research requirements, and Silver Lion earnings all seem carefully tuned to push players toward opening their wallets. Instead of playing because it's fun, you end up playing because you've already invested so much time.  The matchmaking is another constant source of frustration. Full uptiers happen far too often, leaving entire lineups feeling obsolete before the match even starts. Some BRs are notorious for being miserable because they're regularly thrown against vehicles with vastly superior technology or ammunition. Instead of balanced games, many matches feel decided by the matchmaker before anyone even spawns.  For a game that's been around for so many years, the lack of meaningful game modes is shocking. Nearly every match boils down to capturing the same circles on the same maps with the same objectives. Naval has been completely abandoned, Ground suffers from it, and Air battles have barely evolved. Imagine all the historical scenarios, dynamic campaigns, PvE missions, or objective-based battles that could exist—but instead we get the same repetitive gameplay loop year after year.  Perhaps the most frustrating part is that the game has enormous potential. The vehicle roster is unmatched, the graphics are excellent, and the damage model can create incredibly satisfying moments. But nearly every system feels built around maximizing frustration and monetization rather than making the game genuinely enjoyable.  War Thunder isn't a bad game because of its core gameplay. It's a bad experience because the developers consistently prioritize grind, monetization, and questionable balance over player enjoyment. it's hard to stay optimistic.  2 out of 10

The main problems (UI and balance) could be fixed relatively easily, but they do not even seem to be planned.  [h2]Pros:[/h2]  - Enduring Confrontation battles are awesome, especially when you are lucky enough to have cooperative teammates. - The damage model is fairly advanced.  [h2]Cons:[/h2]  1) Controls: mouse and keyboard  Aiming vs. observing. In aiming mode, you cannot properly monitor what is happening around you. In third-person view, you cannot aim effectively, at least in RB. If you switch from aiming mode to third-person view and then back again, your aim is off. You also cannot see the distance to the target or how it changes in third-person view, so you really have to stay in aiming mode if you want to hit anything more than about 5 km away. As a result, people constantly bump into each other, while “realistically” taking no damage.  Distance correction. It is unpredictable: you adjust it by one step, but the distance can change by 200, 100, 10, or 0 meters. You never know what it will do.  2) UI  You cannot reliably identify enemy ship types unless you remember them all. At the same time, you can very realistically see the full internal layout of a ship and its crew size from 20 miles away. So the easiest solution is to use a table matching crew size to ship type, but that is not fun at all.  3) Balance  Premium vehicles are overpowered. Compare USS Arkansas, a premium 6.7 battleship with 12-inch guns and 280 / 280 / 114 mm citadel armor, with something like Parizhskaya Kommuna, a 6.7 battleship with 12-inch guns and 50 / 225 / 75 mm citadel armor. Arkansas can penetrate Kommuna, but not the other way around; still, they have the same BR.  4) Maps  At least at BR 7.0 and above, most battles end up on very realistic circular maps with no cover. You do not need tactics or skill there; you just need guns and armor. Even if you dislike or ban those maps, you still end up playing them because there are so many of them.  My takeaway is this: the people working on the game do not seem to want to be proud of their work. They seem to want to sell you premium vehicles for €80 each. As of now, this is not a game; it is a waste of time and money.

A premium vehicle has been structured to the point that we not only want the tanks but often players feel like they need them in order to do the grind. The average premium cost as much as full priced AAA games, this is just scummy. Premium time is also becoming more needed as economy changes can put the average in a place they lose currency each and every game.  2. Maps have been the same with minimal negative changes throughout the years. The balancing of maps has gotten far worse over the years and with the slow updates to them players are often just camping some exploit that gaijin hasnt noticed since no one there seems to play the actual game.  3. Naval needs a total overhaul. I am not saying it needs to be deleted because naval has so much potential. However the map issue list above even more apparent in naval. You should not just load in and be facing the entire team in a open area in close range. The nations currently in the game are also missing their naval trees even after some nations have been in the game for a decade.  4. Helicopters are greatly missing the love from gaijin resulting in a lack of love from us players. For instance they have been in the game for years and years and they lack dedicated modes like the rest of the vehicles outside of the broken multi br sim mode. Their use in Ground matches has become a negative experience because of reasons listed above spilling into their design structure.  5. The grind. I know as a "free to play" game that they make their money from the grind. If the grind is hard and they can make money by makin it easier then they will. Many games use this model these days. However the grind has gotten to the point it is almost impossible without premium. The game encourages us to grind multiple tech trees and yet to do this without spending hundreds of dollars would take the normal player a crazy amount of time. It has been said before but right now the grind is the game instead of it simply being for enjoyment.  6. Sim. Realistic is the most common form of the game when it comes to the grind and player count. It is positioned as the middle ground between sim and arcade level of play. For context, I'm very passionate about aviation and flight sims of all kinds. MSFS, Xplane 12, DCS, Falcon BMS, Il2 Cliffs of Dover, Great Battles and 1946, Combat Sim 1, 2 and 3. So this will be a lot more of a review of the aviation side of War Thunder.  War Thunder was fun, and has its moments. The ease in which you can just select a plane and hop into a battle is really nice, especially without the need of getting a joystick, or any flight sim eqiupment. Early WWII aviation is fun, easy to grind and generally a decent start.  But I do not reccomend this game. To anyone.  Even if you don't care about competing. Even if you don't mind just buying your one favorite vehicle and just playing that.  I started to simply have an easy way to play my favorite aircraft of WWII, particularly the P-51 Mustangs. (DID YOU KNOW THE P51 WON THE WARRRR?)   I didn't mind that it was not the meta. Did not mind getting shot down a lot. Did not care even for the grind.  But what drove me away was the lack of caring from Gajin.  Gajin has HORRIBLE balancing for their vehicles. Even in low tiers, there are a couple of extremely overpowered vehicles that simply destroy matches. There's getting shot down because of a mistake you made, then there is you die no matter what you do simply because of the OP vehicle you faced.   Then there is the egregious pricing for premium vehicles. Sixty to eighty dollars for induvidual aircraft! For context, full study level sims and study level aircraft in other flight sim games are just as much. The difference being that there is exrtodinary detail and systems in other aircraft from other games. Whereas War Thunder asks the same price for a flying model.  The grind can absolutely get to you, even if you try to ignore it. Because the other team that has simply better aircraft that will tempt you to get premium aircraft.  The mechanics of this game seem like they are meant to foster an addictive cycle. Each time I try to walk from War Thunder, I'm drawn back into playing more.  I do not reccomend this game at all. Any other game I listed above is more worth your time. Or read some Osprey Publishing books on these aircraft. Or buy some RC WWII airplanes. Anything, but this game.  Do not buy into what The Snail offers.

Played this game for years and I still love the core gameplay, but Gaijin really tests my patience. First off, stop locking cool/iconic vehicles behind premium just because they're popular. We all know what that is — it's a cash grab, plain and simple.  And speaking of premiums — the prices are flat out ridiculous. We're talking $50-70+ for a single vehicle sometimes. For a game that already nickel-and-dimes you with premium time, boosters, and a slow grind, charging that much for one tank or plane is just greedy.  Second, the silence. Bug reports, QoL suggestions, mode requests... it all goes into a black hole. Doesn't matter how reasonable the ask is, you just don't get a response. After a while it stops feeling like an accident. Third, there's a clear pattern in who gets the good stuff first. Best SPAA? Goes to one side. Armor upgrades like volumetric? Same side, every time. Random niche weapon systems that barely have public info? Also that side. You start to notice it after enough patches.  Fourth — and this is the one that really gets me — the bug report standards are not consistent. Sometimes a vehicle gets buffed off what feels like a rumor. Other times you can hand over full documentation, sources, the works, and still get told "not enough proof" or "working as intended." Funny how the side that keeps getting nerfed for no real reason is usually the same side. And then there's the grind. New vehicles every update, sure, but the RP curve never gets touched. Helicopters are a joke at this point — basically unreachable for most players. Ground grind vs air grind isn't even close either; ground gets shafted on rewards.  Honestly, I'd take ONE big update that adds zero new vehicles and just fixes the backlog — bugs, balance, grind, premium pricing, the works — over another shiny new tank or jet. Then follow it with an update that's just new modes. Would genuinely make this game so much better.  But yeah, we all know that's not happening anytime soon.

TL;DR Gaijin has shifted from making a vehicle combat sim to a cash grab, trapping new players who buy high-tier premiums just to skip the horrible grind the developers refuse to fix. The game is plagued by predatory "bait-and-switch" balancing, where overpowered vehicles are sold for hype and then nerfed. alongside severe BR compression, hollow major updates, terrible battle passes, and neglect of minor nations like Sweden, italy, and Israel. Predatory monetization and refusal to listen to the player base are killing the experience, resulting in a firm "do not recommend."   As a player with over 1,600 hours and upwards of $2,000 invested into premium time, vehicles, and marketplace mistakes (like sinking $130 into a VFW I can’t even get rid of), it is incredibly frustrating to watch the state of this game.My biggest issue isn't the money spent—it’s the developers actively refusing to listen to the player base or fix core game loops. When I started playing around April of 2023, overpowered premiums already existed, but recent updates have shifted Gaijin’s focus entirely from making a vehicle combat sim to a cash grab.  The New Player Trap & The Horrible Grind I don't blame players for buying high-tier premiums; they simply want to skip the horrible, dragged-out grind that Gaijin refuses to change because they profit off it. New players are given a few bot games and a terrible tutorial, only to be immediately thrown into the deep end of the ocean and told to swim. They have to face seal-clubbing Level 100 veterans dominating the low tiers, which naturally pushes them to open their wallets just to bypass the misery. Because of this, it's an everyday occurrence to see brand-new Level 8 players running full premium lineups featuring blatantly overpowered, undertiered vehicles like the 2S38 and BMPT-72.  Predatory Balancing & Bait-and-Switch Gaijin’s entire approach to balancing is completely predatory. They systematically release brand-new, blatantly broken and overpowered vehicles that dominate matches. They let players buy up the hype, but once the sales window slows down and the hype dies out, they hit the vehicle with a massive nerf or an uptier—essentially making all those people lose their money and rendering the vehicle a shell of what they paid for.    Adding Unwanted "Slop" On top of ignoring actual vehicular content, Gaijin has started pumping out tone-deaf slop that absolutely no one asked for. Stuff like the "Senrai Maidens" deco packs completely shatters the aesthetic of what is supposed to be a realistic vehicle combat sim. im not opposed to having fun with your cosmetics and enjoying the game for how you want but gaijin forcing you to pay 70$ for what essentially is a TT tank with a skin and body pillow. It just goes to show they are completely out of touch, prioritizing cheaply (AI) made but sold high cosmetics over what their dedicated player base actually wants.  Major Updates & Hollow Additions The major updates have been absolutely horrible lately. The recent updates drop barely a handful of vehicles, and none of them are actually things the community has been begging for for years. Instead, we get uninspired additions, copy-paste export vehicles, and battle passes that completely suck, offering uninteresting rewards while long-standing tanks that ruin entire matchmaker brackets (like the T58) are ignored.  BR Compression & Neglect of Minor Nations Compression has completely ruined certain parts of the game, leaving vehicles without stabilizers or thermals to regularly fight heavily stabilized monsters equipped with top-tier optics. On top of that, trees that don't generate massive premium profits for Gaijin are left in the dust. Sweden is my main, and it feels overwhelmingly neglected in terms of engaging new additions. We get a lackluster AA system, export AAs, and a new Gripen model, but the actual tank tech tree still feels hollow. The Strv 122 might be an excellent vehicle, but the grind up to that point is miserable unless you shill out $60 for a CV90105, which itself leaves much to be desired. The core foundation of War Thunder is great, but predatory balancing, bait-and-switch mechanics, refusal to decompress BRs, hollow updates, and aggressive monetization are killing the experience. I cannot recommend this game in its current state.

I remember my first time playing this game. It was awesome. Popping into a tank to learn how to shoot things, seeing them explode up into flames, and learning aircraft combat was a blast. I absolutely loved it.  And I never felt anything close to that way again.  The dev support for this game is genuinely awful. There's so many problems with just the core gameplay mechanics. Sometimes they're obvious like ghost shells (or volumetric for those of you who have already played), but there's inherent design flaws in many of the game mode types as well, most of which are just "capture the point", or "kill everyone", which usually doesn't actually work well.   The community IS listened to! But ONLY when it's positive feedback (which is rare). For example, the new Nuclear Thunder gamemode (which does have a lot of promising potential actually) was really liked by the community, having for the most part really enjoyable gameplay, except for a few issues. IMO, I've seen the biggest issue for most players being the cracked and unbalanced AAA (some teams have AAA that does basically nothing, others can spawnkill you). And the only AAA "nerfs" just like, make it actually reload. I think they've actually gotten stronger, not weaker.  So, putting dev support aside, how is the actual game? Most of the game in theory is kinda fun, but nearly all of the fun is stripped away because of one thing: the grind.  For me, it's taken me 800 hours to reach top-tier US aircraft (and only one, not even the full tree) and about mid-high tier tanks in that nation, about a third(ish) of it with premium (effectively doubling game rewards). That's over a month if you were to play it straight. It takes a near eternity to actually get anything later game, but that's not even the biggest problem with how it's set up.  Most games cost you the in-game currency (silver lions, SL) to play, as damaged vehicles need to be repaired with SL (or in some modes, you have to use SL to spawn in). This adds actual risk to each game. If you don't perform well, or just crash your plane and die, you effectively went negative that round. Now for the most part, if you're semi-decent you'll recoup enough SL to not actually go negative. But the biggest problem is that with every game you know you have to perform, and to get kills, because if you don't, you're losing SL. This does help players be a bit more serious in the game, I guess, but it comes at the expense of genuinely having fun. It's way harder to have fun when money's at stake.  And then as well, the game is just filled with learning curves that the game doesn't help you through. There are very few resources for actual strategy, and although some of the tutorials for mechanics are getting better, they still generally suck.  TL;DR:  - The dev support sucks as they don't listen to the community - There's inherent game design flaws - The fact that you could lose in-game currency each game drains the fun - It's often a bit of a learning curve - You get stuck in the grind  I do think this game has a lot of potential. I think this could excel really well. But as the saying goes, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it", and right now, it's making money, so Gaijin isn't fixing it.  Now, if you DO still want to play the game, here's my advice: 1. Do not rush. That sounds counter-intuitive - it's a grindy game so you should get it over faster, right? Well, no. That's the exact mindset that makes you prioritize the progress over the experience. Enjoy it for what it is. Don't buy a tier VIII vehicle just to jump to the top (the learning curve will be REALLY ROUGH). Now, this will definitely take a while, and if you don't want it to take a while, don't play the game.  2. Look up YouTube tutorials. There definitely are YT tutorials for playing the game and learning how to do it. If you're confused about a specific mechanic, look it up. If you're wondering how to play better, look it up (but please do learn how the game works before you worry about being good).   3. Play every major nation (USA, USSR, Germany, and any others you want to throw in) through Rank II before choosing which one to play/grind. I didn't do this, but I wish I did. This will allow you to learn more or less how the nations work, and also how strategy and the game in general works. I'd even recommend going through Rank III on a couple just to get a better feel for the game and the nations.  4. The moment you feel like you want to buy premium/spend money, quit. If you're considering one of those, it's probably because you feel like progress is too slow. That's what I've been warning you about - it's grindy, it takes forever, and that grindy feel takes out the fun.  Again, I do think this game has potential. I think there's a lot of value it has, and I want to see it become the best version of what it can be. But for now, it's not. The devs don't listen to complaints - only support when it rarely exists. It's buggy. It's grindy. The "F" in War Thunder stands for fun. Once the game is genuinely enjoyable again, I'll be writing a really good review. But that's only if I can start enjoying it again.  (Also steam says I have 788 hours when reviewing, but I actually have 809. Idk what that's about)

Short version: I honestly cannot recommend this game to anyone. The Snail foreclosed my home.  Long version: I've played this game for several years at this point. I am at the point in a couple tech trees that, when I had started, just did not exist. I know I'm not the only one who's had this experience, and truthfully I barely played the high- to top-tiers. There have been a lot of issues I've had with the game, previously that I've tolerated, for context I am largely a ground main, despite the copy-and-paste tanks and trees, the general disregard for WW2 to early Cold War era vehicles for the most modern vehicles (which, unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars, you will not ever see), the overpowered premiums (cough PT-76/57 cough) and the use of player stats to balance vehicles (who else remembers 5.7 Tiger E/Panther A?), despite it all I tolerated it, made fun memories with friends as a squad, recorded a video every once and a while. l tolerated it, there would be genuinely good changes here and there, and I'll be first to admit that sunk-cost played something of a role. I've played air RB up to the first jets as well,  and remember the more dynamic game modes they've removed. Essentially both ground and air RB are team death matches. At this point in time, I must urge anyone who is thinking of downloading it to save themselves from the frustration and the grind. If you play air RB, you're looking at spending 1/2 to 3/4 of the match climbing to altitude, a couple minutes actually fighting, and you may or may not get a kill, two if you're particularly lucky. Ground RB? Because of the map designs, you might just get sniped leaving spawn, and if you make it out, it can be pretty fun until you hear the bells tolling in the form of an aircraft engine. The further into the tech-tree you go, the more likely it is you'll be CAS'd (revenge bombed or otherwise), up to the point where you'll be more likely to die from a helicopter, jet CAS, or drone than an actual tank. Given that it is a *tank* mode, most people aren't running a dedicated SPAA in their lineup at all, much less as their primary vehicle. Most SPAAs that aren't broken (Leopard 40/70, Coelian, BTR-ZD, and the 30mm NATO SPAA in the 8.0-9.0 range come to mind) are not capable of destroying contemporary ground targets, and many are difficult to use in their intended role. CAS is extremely easy to spawn, a couple years ago Spookston made a video demonstrating that you could get a kill with CAS in 1:50 after match start, depending on the map. There's a reason why the meme about looking inside your tank game and find nothing but planes is so prevalent. Now, in the year of our Lord 2026, not only do we have all these issues with the game itself and the manner in which it is aggressively monetized, but with the new copy-and-paste anime pack they've started selling AI generated content (that they were too lazy to remove the watermark on) and at AAA pricing. There are a lot of things you can buy for 80ish USD, including most AAA games. What is certainly not worth that cost is a cheaply made, AI-generated, mid-voice acted gooner pack with camos far inferior to the ones you could find on the forums (which are free) for tanks you can just find in the normal tech-tree. Not to mention how they broke the at first extremely popular Nuclear Thunder, which may at some point come back in that broken state, and then will complain that no one plays the game mode as an excuse to eventually remove it. As someone who as spent way too much time on this game, who has spent money on this game, save yourselves. The company will not improve the game, and in my opinion it will continue on this downward trend. The game itself has plenty of players, it's in a healthy state in that aspect, but it is a dysfunctional game, the single major hit Gaijin has had, and I think it is too much of a cash cow for them to meaningfully attempt to make the necessary changes to make the game enjoyable. The game is a decade old with essentially a single game mode for ground battles. Few folks play the caps because that's a great way to telegraph your location to the 1000kg bomb headed straight for your forehead, which turns the match into a 5-25 minute TDM, with teammates that can range from absolutely cracked to someone who bought a premium pack 10 minutes ago and is playing their first match ever. I cannot stress this enough, do *not* play this game.
