So given that a large part of the community and a bunch of big WT creators are currently trying to collectively voice their dissatisfactions with the game, I thought I might actually take the time to review a game that I have been playing for ages now and have a love-hate relationship with.  [i][u] Please not that despite the current wave of negative reviews, my review is not influenced by them, it just pushed me to actually write it. What I'm criticizing is stuff that my friends and I have been criticizing in our game sessions for a while. [/u][/i]  [h2] The Positive [/h2] [list] [*]Can be a lot of fun, having a good match in War Thunder is extremely satisfying [*]The vehicles are modelled with a high degree of detail [*]There are so many vehicles to unlock [*]Some of the maps are really nice to play [*]Matchmaking is generally really quick and there is a large player base [*]Lower Tier is a lot of fun[spoiler], unless you only play against T-34's and Panzer IV's [/spoiler] [*]The addition of daily universal backups has been one of the best things they've done in a while. [/list]  [h2] The Negative [/h2] [list] [*]Ground battles only have one game mode with different flavours: capture and defend one point, capture and defend three points, capture the enemy point while defending yours. [*]GROUND BATTLES have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ planes in them. I can't recall how often I was in the middle of an intense battle, only to have it ruined by another player bombing me from his small-♥♥♥♥-energy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plane. [*]Compared to ground realistic battles, air realistic battles feel like a scam. You only get one plane for the entire round and it takes forever to even reach the enemy. [*]There are a lot of vehicles that feel overpowered for their battle rating (a lot of them are russian vehicles, but not exclusively). Playing against them is just not fun. [*]The map rotation is abysmal, there are so many cool maps that you could play but most of them are never selected. Instead you're put in a rotation of maybe 3-5 maps and have to play them over and over again. And these maps are not even that good. This game really has potential, but after playing it for a while, I can't really recommend it to any new players, based on the direction the developers are taking with it. Here's the good, the bad, and my recommendations for the players and the devs.  The Good: - The initial grind from Rank I to Rank III is likely the most fun I've had, though it could be due to seal clubbing new players. You research vehicles and upgrades quickly, and have a blast developing the tech trees. - Like other multplayer games, it's a lot more fun when you're playing with friends and coordinating rushes or defensive lines in Ground or Air Realistic Battles.  The Bad: - The playerbase, especially in Air RB. Because friendly fire isn't disabled in this mode, so teammates will crash into or shoot you for no real reason at the start of a match. - If you play with German teammates in NA, good luck winning the match (all wehraboos suck at the game). - Lately, there has been a lack of interesting event and battlepass vehicles. It seems like the developers are more interested in making money selling copy-paste premium vehicles instead of filling out the gaps in existing tech trees. - Gaijin has also used Gemini's AI tools to make textures for their vehicles in the latest Senrai Maiden Premium Pack, as well as other newly added vehicles. You can tell by how the Gemini star logo can be found on the lower right of the corner. - Volumetric armor effects, and how the shape of what you're shooting can cause some shots to bounce off armor harmlessly, even when they have a good chance of hitting. - HE shell explosions for HESH rounds make their performance inconsistent. - Shot types like APCR, or AP, APBC, APCBC often spall or do more damage in real life, but do little damage in game comparatively. - Minor nations like Japan, Sweden, France, and especially Israel have immense repair costs, despite these vehicles having similar performance or worse performance to other nations.  Recommendations (for players): - Play this game in short bursts. It's easy to get tilted if you have a few bad matches in a row, but at the end of the day, it's just a game. Don't burn yourself out trying to grind out the next vehicle, dailies, or the event vehicles. - I don't recommend you start with minor nations like Italy or France, since their vehicles are more difficult to play with lesser armor, mobility, or firepower. Starting with a major nation like the USSR, USA, Britain, or Germany would be a better bet. - Do not buy low effort premium vehicles, as this incentivizes Gaijin to get away with pumping out low effort content if it sells well.   Recommendations (for the developers): - Gaijin approves dubious changes to Russian vehicles with limited or first party documenation, yet reject bugfixes or revisions to NATO bloc vehicles, even when unclassified, reputable documentation is used to confirm improvements to specifications. You can't have it both ways. - Gaijin seems to be investing significant effort using AI in their workflow, instead working with artists, modellers, programmers to release interesting vehicles that take more effort and research. If you invest more time making better, more interesting content, you can increase the playerbase and incentivize players to stay.

This is the first review I write on steam for any game ever.  I have played the game since at least 2015 and I loved it for its realistic and complex simulation of flying and general combat physics. It was amazing to see the game develop over time, with new combat mechanics and improvements of the graphics and simulation being the most relevant steps for the value and enjoyability of the game. Then, during the last years, the game stopped developing and started degenerating.  What was largely left out of the game's evolution was gameplay. Arcade and Realistic Battles are short games where you mostly fight for capture points on small maps (ground) or climb for quite a while towards the middle of an ambiguous large map where you will witness a mostly short clash of uncoordinated planes in a team deathmatch (air), none of which (!) resemble a realistic military confrontation. Simulator battles on ground is the same without HUD, while the air simulator battle is the only game mode where (only) air vehicles are used the way they were intended to be, but which is at the same is too difficult to be recommendable for anyone but enthusiasts. Simulator Battles are the only game mode where I felt lasting interest at least for some time, although even those modes feel neglected and vastly underdeveloped.  The creation of new gamemodes has been one of the biggest concerns for the playerbase for years (!) now. Gaijin does not seem to acknowledge the issue. The company focuses heavily to create ever new vehicle models into the thousands to scatter all over the tech trees where they do or do not have a right to be. At the same time most of the new modern vehicles don't even work on the small maps and with available game modes in combat situations, which they were never designed for. There is little space for individuality, creativity and in the end, often little realism. The grind for ever new vehicles distracts from the fact that the actual gameplay becomes ever more stale and degenerate the further you progress.  I am describing the issue honestly and as differentiated as I can. I factually stopped playing the game a long time despite its incredible potential. If relevant changes are made, I will pick the game up again gladly.

English below  *GERMAN* Von einem guten Spiel zur Pay-to-Win-Hölle  Von „Wir wollen sehr nah an der Realität sein“ zu „Wir wollen nur euer Geld“. Ungefähr bis zum Release des BMPT hätte ich hier noch einen Daumen nach oben gegeben.  War Thunder war lange Zeit ein wirklich tolles Spiel, das mich mit seinem Realismus im Vergleich zu Arcade-Shootern wie WoT abgeworben hat. Persönlich finde ich den Grind gar nicht so schlimm; es ist meist eine Achterbahnfahrt mit Höhen und Tiefen. Mittlerweile überwiegen jedoch die Tiefen, sobald man im BR 11+ ankommt.  Seit dem Release des BMPT geht es einfach bergab. Dieser Panzer ist die Definition von Pay-to-Win. In der Realität ist dieses „Ding“, nach allem was bisher bekannt ist, ein ziemlicher Fehlschlag. Die Läufe wackeln bei jedem Schuss und die Präzision ist dadurch ein Witz – nicht aber in unserem „realitätsnahen“ War Thunder. Hier mutiert dieser Panzer meiner Meinung nach zu einem Über-Panzer im Vergleich zu anderen. Man begegnet diesem Ungetüm in nahezu jeder Runde, in der Russland im Gegnerteam ist. Das Schöne daran: Wenn man sich mal die Spielerprofile der BMPT-Nutzer ansieht, sitzen da häufig die größten „Kartoffeln“ drin. Aber kein Problem, der Panzer ist ja broken – weil Russland ;). Generell habe ich mittlerweile das Gefühl, dass gerade Russland im Spiel viel besser behandelt wird als andere Nationen, was vielleicht an der Herkunft des Publishers liegt.  Wenn ich mittlerweile die Panzer der Nationen vergleiche, gibt es fast nur noch Copy-Paste. Ein neuer „Panzer“ für Großbritannien ist ein Abrams – wie toll. Oder auch die Einführung der M44 für quasi jede Nation. Also wirklich, Gaijin, allein Deutschland hätte da so viele bessere Alternativen gehabt. Generell gäbe es eine so große Auswahl an Panzern, die man ins Spiel bringen könnte, aber stattdessen bekommen wir Premium-Panzer, die einfach nur eine leicht abgewandelte Version aus dem Forschungsbaum sind – und manchmal ist es sogar nur ein neuer Skin. Man bekommt einfach immer mehr das Gefühl, dass die Community hier nur noch gemolken wird.  Das Thema der immer noch viel zu starken CAS (Close Air Support) will ich hier gar nicht erst groß anschneiden. Bitte fügt einfach einen reinen Panzer-Modus für diejenigen ein, die das spielen wollen, oder setzt ein Limit für Flugzeuge und Helikopter – ähnlich wie bei WoT mit der Artillerie. Auch könnte man meiner Meinung nach das Kartensystem überarbeiten. Es gibt so viele Karten, die man bannen möchte, weil sie einfach unausgeglichen sind oder keinen Spaß machen, aber man hat ja leider nur einen Ban.  Aber es ist nicht alles schlecht. Seit ich mit War Thunder angefangen habe, gab es in meinen Augen auch viele gute Entwicklungen. Zum Beispiel, dass die Panzermodule mehr Details bekommen haben, wie etwa die Stromversorgung, oder dass der Stabilisator nun ein eigenständiges System ist.   *ENGLISH* From a good game to a Pay-to-Win hell  From "we want to be as close to reality as possible" to "we just want your money." Up until the release of the BMPT, I probably would have still given this a thumbs up.  For a long time, War Thunder was a really beautiful game that won me over with its realism compared to arcade shooters like WoT. Personally, I don't find the grind too bad; it's mostly a rollercoaster of highs and lows. Lately, however, it's mostly lows once you reach BR 11+.  Ever since the release of the BMPT, things have just been going downhill. This tank is the definition of pay-to-win. In reality, this "thing"—based on what is currently known—is a failure. The barrels wobble with every shot, making its accuracy a joke, but not in our "realistic" War Thunder. Here, in my opinion, this tank turns into an overpowered monster compared to everything else. You get to face this behemoth in almost every match where Russia is on the enemy team. The funny thing is, if you look at the player profiles of those using this tank, it's often the biggest "potatoes" driving it. But no problem, the tank is broken anyway, because Russia ;). Generally, I get the feeling lately that Russia is treated much better than other nations, which might be due to the publisher's origin.  When I compare the tanks across nations these days, it's almost entirely copy-paste. A new "tank" for Great Britain is an Abrams—how great. Or just adding the M44 to almost every nation. Premium tanks that are just slightly different versions of tech-tree variants, or sometimes just a reskin. You just increasingly get the feeling that the community is only being milked.  I don't even want to get started on the issue of the still overpowered CAS (Close Air Support). Please, just add a tank-only mode for those who want to play it, or put a limit on planes and helicopters like WoT did with artillery. Also, I think the map system could use a rework. There are so many maps you'd want to ban because they are simply unbalanced or not fun, but unfortunately, you only get one ban.  But it's not all bad. Since I started playing War Thunder, there have been a lot of good changes in my eyes too—for example, the tank modules getting more detailed, like the power supply, or the stabilizer now being a standalone system.

Tanks If you like historical tanks, then this is the game for you. You start with early tanks and lots of options. With some time, you will have access to tanks like the Tiger or the Sherman. The hit playback shows you what you damaged and what compartments of the enemy tank is destroyed. I really like this feature.  But please beware that when you wish to play with modern vehicles you will have to play a lot. It’s a true grinding game. And the only way to get to a higher tier of tanks (and other vehicles) is to play A LOT. I’ve played for ca. 500 hours and I have not yet reached the 12.7 BR tanks. You could buy your way to this level, but this costs about 60 euros. And in my opinion, its not worth it. You will have one tank (or plane/battleship) in your lineup. And you will play against strong players who know the game better.   Planes Now there are also planes, helicopters, and battleships. Planes are a great addition to the game. And in ranked games you can take your planes (and helicopters) to tank battles. Planes offer great gameplay and dogfights feel fun and tactical. Nothing more is to be said about planes.   Helicopters Helicopters are incredibly bad. The learning curve is insane. And when you research your first helicopter you will be shot down by AA fire before you get a hit on a tank. You can still enjoy helicopters in arcade battles at high BR battles. But in ranked battles it sucks.   Naval Naval battles feel, at least to me, like trying to manage an entire ship at once and always failing. You’re busy steering, range finding, shooting (all guns or volley), repairing and playing the objective. Its not fun. Perhaps you love ships and this type of gameplay. If that’s the case beware that this is the lowest played mode in War Thunder.

Gaijin is a company that constantly talks about realism and accurate portrayal of vehicles. However, they blatantly ignore sources given to them by users to justify changes to vehicles, instead implementing balance decisions on a whim or based on "documents" that are never disclosed with the playerbase. Your favorite vehicle is underperforming: the gun takes too long to load, it's missing 200 horsepower, or the turn rate is too slow. You scour the internet, finding an official advertisement from the manufacturer stating the given value. You submit it in a ticket. A community manager closes it on a whim. Or it contradicts Gaijin's own special calculation for a given value. Or they just say "this isn't possible because X is similar and can't do what Y claims." Even the more influential figures in the community, like YouTubers and streamers are often subject to the same treatment.   It wouldn't be an issue if Gaijin just publicly stated that they base changes on how the vehicle is performing (or, more likely, what an arbitrary win rate/KDR spreadsheet implies, which is skewed by individual player skill) rather than insisting that players can make a difference by submitting information. Time and time again players have been frustrated by this tedious process, which leads to the infamous document leaks where disgruntled individuals submit classified information because of Gaijin's stringent (and seemingly random) requirements for sources. You can't just show them a reputable secondary source. You need a flight manual signed by a general before they even look at it, and even then, they might just deny it or completely misrepresent what it says by using a random value from it, like when they nerfed the M41's turret traverse rate by using the MINIMUM (slowest) turn rate as its HIGHEST or the M1128's total ENGAGEMENT time as its reload time.  Further, Gaijin has leaned heavily into so-called copy-paste and low effort premiums. Nations are becoming increasingly homogenous as every release sees some new NATO standard vehicle or similar added to several tech trees, which makes matches monotonous and confusing as encounters become repetitive and the game's soundscape, which is very important to situational awareness, becomes clogged with identical engine noises (when the game's sound system decides to work at all.) Premium vehicles have also become egregious. Updates increasingly feature more and more premium vehicles to be purchase with in-game currency rather than being added to the tech tree where they can be received for free through gameplay. Players buy their way to the best vehicles, then proceed to stomp the enemy in cases of particularly powerful ones (BMPT and BMPT-72 come to mind) or they skip ahead to higher tiers in the game without learning fundamentals, leaving after a few frustrating deaths and abandoning their team. Vehicles have also been recycled as premiums, such as in Gaijin's new Senrai Maidens IP, which feels like you took every vaguely combat related anime and threw it into a blender, leaving a homogenous, discolored paste that you then painted onto a vehicle already in the game. Which is funny, because Gaijin has been using AI to generate assets, such as when the Gemini watermark was seen on camouflage patterns and assets associated with the Senrai Maiden vehicles.  All in all, a game that can be fun and offers a wide variety of vehicles is being increasingly hindered by a profit-oriented and, at times, seemingly vengeful company that gives sloppy, half-hearted responses to community concerns while selling them over-priced garbage. Unless things take a turn for the better, don't get into it, otherwise you'll be spending months grinding away or hundreds of dollars to reach the things Gaijin so heavily advertises.

Developers are immune to listening to feedback and taking accountability for poor judgement and decisions. In order to balance vehicles, they accept unclassified documents posted to forums as real-world evidence to be implemented into their games. However, the developers being Russian, are quick to accept a napkin drawing showcasing the glory of a Russian vehicle, while endlessly dispute, debate and maneuver around accepting a declassified source from an official NATO entity. This constant repositioning of goalposts has made it so that nations like China and Russia, technologically weaker in real life than their NATO counterparts, can field ahistorical vehicles and if a new technology is added in the game, the Russians and Chinese get it before the NATO nations, skewing game balance in their favour for at least an update before player complaints are finally listened to, or the developers sweep it under the rug.  Furthermore, the game has reached a state where almost every new vehicle every update is a copy + paste premium that costs more than buying any AAA video game on the Steam homepage right now. The variance between tech trees in lower tiers has reached a point of convergence in higher tiers which makes the game incredibly dull. Lack of CAS balance, new maps and game modes has tarnished the game's lustre and lots of players now realize that without change, this game is on the road to death, just like WOWS before it.  However, it's not all bad. Low tiers are still fun and there have been good changes made in the past (albeit only after player review-bombing and boycotting) so to a casual player, the game can still be enjoyable. The only issue with this is the lack of an updated game tutorial. The learning curve is steep and if a player isn't committed to learning the game, it is hard for them to come back. Personally, it took me a number of youtube videos and tutorials from friends to learn the game enough that it was enjoyable to continue queuing. This is a necessary change to ensure casual players come back to the game.  Gaijin needs to realize that the only reason why their game is popular is only because they have cornered the market in military vehicular simulations. Other offerings like WOT are too arcadey, while games like DCS have too steep of a learning curve for the more casual player. Believing that you can continue to disrespect players, refuse suggestion, and gaslight your customers into thinking that their complaints are baseless will only lessen the grip on the monopoly you currently enjoy within this corner of gaming and guarantee the end of the game that we all love.  These were just some quick thoughts about the game, please read other reviews and do your own research before committing to trying it out.

Do not start playing this game.  [h2] Long Review [/h2]  I have no idea how new players would even approach this game anymore. If you play air, the higher the tier the more it is full of premium planes in a deathmatch repeating over and over into a grey slime. If you play ground, I'm not sure how you even want to play past the first few hours. Planes bomb your sherman or t34 with almost impunity. A guy who looks more like a moving terrarium (using items you can no longer acquire for a decade) sits twiddling his thumbs until you decide to push forward. It has the same excitement as trench warfare. Many of the strongest tanks and jets are locked behind the cost of a full new game, at which point, why play this one?  I know this because this is what I do to other people. At the lower beginning tiers, in order to farm for a limited time ground vehicle, I will take out a plane. It was only acquirable years before you, potential new player, made your account. You can't get it anymore. I will get 5-8 kills with it regularly. Then I will take a back up spawn of it, and do it again. There's very little you can do to stop me unless you leave your vehicle and take another which is specifically designed to counter mine. However it will likely be useless against most of the vehicles you face.  Does that sound fun? There are people much better than me at the game, they have even better vehicles I passed on. There is no elo or mmr to divide the best players from the worst, and the learning curve is steep. The only positive I can think of is that if you download it now, you'll get to seal club the poor saps who come after you. But it's already been over 13 years. What hope do you have?  If you somehow make it through that filter, all the way to top tier. You will find that your games are even less engaging. In ground, a significant proportion take one high rank vehicle they paid for, die, then leave for the next game. Potential opponents gone, the game slows, a guy fires a missile from 20km away, your tank explodes. You would think that teaches you to move through cover, through buildings. Many maps have kilometers of open field, some are almost exclusively open fields. What is your solution? If you play air, as mentioned previously, you will your games move from engaging methodical fights against planes of varying strengths and weaknesses, to a missile furball where you face the same jet over and over again, looking at you colombian su-30mk2. Without it, there would be less players, longer queue times, fundamental issues in game mode variety, irrational map designs that the solution for was reducing the traction to sliding on ice, power creep updates for more than a decade, increasing difference between the worst and the best vehicle at a given matchmaking bracket through compression of those brackets because achieving higher tiers is exponentially difficult.  Finally, once you have achieved this high rank, if you did it by learning as opposed to doing your best pachycephalosaurus impression against the brick wall, you will find it's not even particularly engaging. You seek ways to handicap yourself so that fights against the average player, who has a K/D of .66, are fun. You can immediately see how eventually you can't handicap yourself enough even by using unguided rockets instead of your guns. There is no victory here, your elitism of achieving what few decide to do isn't excellence, it's folly. The fruit is hollow. The problem starts with the economy and how grinding works. As a player that has never bought premium, or, rarely did (maybe for 1 or 2 weeks in total) and having made my way through the entire US Tech Tree, it gets ridiculous. Like, WAYYY too ridiculous on how much you've got to grind.  To begin the problems, its a long grind, the games don't give you a lot of RP, nowadays its a bit better if you're good at the game and can manage to kill 2-3 enemies every game. And, at those ranks it honestly feels like a lot of the time you're just getting the downgraded version, compared to the other techtrees that get stronger ones, even if, that vehicle, originally wasn't from their place.  Overall, the game is fun, but not in its current state, with the devs taking a political stance catered thowards russian and chinese players, a lot of stuff is missing or plainly innacurate, and every single update thats coming out is starting to feel less and less unique, with new vehicles barely changing compared to older ones, and a ton of premium vehicles added.

Originally fun concept, great models and selection of vehicles, has the potential to be one of the best games available. The game modes are still the exact same as when it launched, except instead of WW2 tanks and aircraft the game is now primarily focused on modern era vehicles with the ability to kill each other 10's of kilometers away. This doesn't work. The game needs new life added to it if it wants to keep emphasising modern vehicles, or it will die in spectacular fashion. Old maps and game modes are still fun for most tanks and aircraft before 1970, but as you progress towards modern missiles, laser rangefinders and standoff capabilities it becomes extremely stale and boring. The game essentially has only one major mode, realisitic battles, however this 'realisim' sees one team of modern era tanks blasting through the entire map and camping spawns within 5 minutes of the game starting, or hordes of fighters punting obnoxious numbers of missiles at each other without any actual objective except 'kill the red ones', bombers, strike aircraft, anti air and SHIPS are all essentially useless and serve no place in 5 minute team deathmatch/elimination. At this point, the only visible reason Gaijin have refused to add any more full time game modes, better top teir maps, or actual combined arms battles with an objective outside of COD team deathmatch is to increase player frustration and incentivise purchasing premium 'meta' vehicles (BMPT). Gaijin just decided to put all their focus into making vehicles, especially premiums because it's what rakes the cash in. Now you would at least think they would be high quality and reasonably priced right? Of course not. Top tier premiums are added every major update, each one costing an arm and a leg and it's just a slightly different looking vehicle from the tech tree, which plays the same way in the same gamemode we have had since launch. The copy pasting vehicles problem to all of the nation's tech trees that get rid each nation's uniqueness is a big issue too.  I honestly wouldn't be surprised if the Gaijin employees don't even play their own game. They spend so much time making these cool vehicles (very expensive for Gaijin to make) just so you can play them in shoddy, flawed as can possibly be maps that ruin the entire experience. Almost every game ends up with one side spawn camping the other which the map design practically encourages players to do by making it incredibly easy, especially in top tier where the battles typically end in like 10-15 minutes because the low level premium buyers quickly die and leave the game which is another problem on its own. CAS in top tier will never not be an absolute mess with jets launching gps bombs from the airfield to wipe the enemy spawn out. There is also no diversity or real objective in the gameplay at all and its just go and drive to ABC every single game inside the tiny little CoD maps. Helicopter specific gamemodes also suck like the PvE one where all you do is shoot at random enemy tanks for an hour where the players with the best helicopter AGMs steals all the kills so you get no rewards at the end.  They need to start by improving the gameplay and maps. The maps need to be bigger and more meaningful (not just open fields) with more real and diverse objectives so that players have goals to achieve and not just driving from point to point. For example, if they created a large scale map that acted as kind of like a giant military operation with lots of different points of interests, they could add AI infantry or vehicles fighting each other across areas in the map and reward the player for assisting friendly forces in securing a small town or outpost or something like in real, joint military combat situations, with enemies trying to complete their own objectives to win and the operation can be determined by land held at the end (attackers took key positions/defenders held attackers back). Maybe even offer specific objectives to different kinds of vehicles such as heavy tanks leading an assault or light vehicles can perform recon or skirmish missions (perhaps give the player options so they can decide what they want to go and do). Planes could then have their own objectives like supporting ground troops across the map and fighting for air superiority (adding AI planes/fodder to attack could help with keeping planes busy and not just focused on killing players). Maybe throw naval in there somewhere for that combined arms feel that Gaijin created or it could receive a more tailored gamemode or something. These are just some quick examples I thought of to make the game more diverse and immersive, giving the game a much better simulation feel and it would compliment the vehicles by giving them a broader scope of combat usefulness as well, rather than CoD tank deathmatch. Also, since these matches would take longer, just give better rewards and not only for player kills so that players are incentivized to complete objectives, rather than just farm player kills.  There are definitely other issues to talk about but now it's time for Gaijin to actually put in some effort and make their game better and not just enslave people with the grind and milk people dry with their overpriced premiums among other money pits.
